articles.title: US Stock trading goes 23 Hours: will the ASX follow?
articles.summary: Webull Securities Australia chief executive Rob Talevski talked with Proactive about the move towards 23-hour trading on major US stock exchanges, what extended trading hours mean for Australian investors and whether the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX) could eventually follow suit. With major US exchanges preparing to expand trading access, Talevski explained how growing demand from retail investors, particularly across the Asia-Pacific region, has helped drive the shift towards nearly round-the-clock trading. He highlighted the role of alternative trading systems such as Blue Ocean Technologies, which helped demonstrate demand for overnight access to US equities. For Australian investors, extended trading hours could provide greater flexibility to respond to market-moving announcements without staying awake during traditional US trading sessions. Talevski also discussed the importance of liquidity, price discovery and bid-ask spreads when trading outside conventional market hours. The discussion explored how Webull's clients are using extended trading access, including actively managing positions, responding to market volatility and trading leveraged or inverse exchange-traded funds (ETFs). Turning to Australia, Talevski assessed whether the ASX could introduce longer trading hours, identifying market size, institutional demand, international investment flows and clearing and settlement arrangements as potential obstacles. He also considered whether competition from Australia's second-largest exchange, now under Canadian ownership, could encourage changes to local trading arrangements. Finally, Talevski outlined the factors investors should consider before trading outside regular market hours, including their broker's execution venues, brokerage costs, available liquidity and the risks associated with overnight trading.
